title: Gating and Snapshotted Kernel Signature Publisher
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement a publish pipeline and gating service that snapshots compiled kernel fingerprints, cryptographically signs kernel artifacts, and publishes stable pins only when telemetry confirms no performance regressions across representative workload shards. This ticket covers the publisher service, a small signer component, and the gating rule set used during canary rollouts for MHA/GQA/MoE model classes.
acceptance_criteria: Snapshot manifest format defined and validated against schema (human-readable + immutable checksum).
Kernel artifacts are produced with reproducible fingerprint (build id, compiler flags, arch tag, checksum) and stored in the artifact registry.
A cryptographic signing component produces verifiable signatures for each snapshot and stores signature metadata alongside manifests.
Gating service evaluates telemetry (latency P95, token throughput, error-rate) from canary runs and emits PASS/FAIL with rationale.
Publishing workflow only promotes a pin to the global registry if gating service returns PASS and manual approver (if required) has signed off.
Rollback path is documented and can be triggered by the console/API within 15 minutes of detection.
technical_design: We will add a new "signature-publisher" microservice that consumes compiled kernel bundles from the build pipeline. Each bundle is normalized into a snapshot manifest that includes canonicalized metadata: model-arch tag (MHA/GQA/MoE), compile profile (quantization, kernel-version), hardware targets, compiler flags, and a SHA-256 of the binary. The signer will use a KMS-backed key to create a signed envelope for the manifest. The publisher will register the snapshot in the pin registry with initial status 'canary'. A separate gating service will subscribe to canary telemetry streams, compute pre-defined regression checks (P95 latency delta <5%, throughput drop <7%, error-rate delta <0.1%), and annotate the snapshot. On PASS, the publisher flips the pin to 'stable' and emits a provenance link. On FAIL, the snapshot remains canary and an automated rollback candidate is queued. The design includes a minimal CLI to re-run gating checks against stored telemetry for audits.
experiments: Local reproducibility run: compile same source with two different build hosts to validate checksum stability (2026-02-25).
Small canary: run signed snapshot for MHA-8B on dedicated canary pool across 3 regions to collect P50/P95 and error metrics (2026-03-03 to 2026-03-05).
GQA stress: inject 50% longer sequences to measure KV cache interactions and ensure gating thresholds tolerate realistic tails (2026-03-07).

2026-02-25 Diego Alvarez: Prototype signer implemented using KMS test key. Checksum stabilized across two build boxes; one outlier due to non-deterministic temp file. Added normalization step to strip build timestamps.

2026-03-04 QA Engineer Jenna Park: Canary MHA-8B run collected 48 hours of telemetry. Observed a 3.8% P95 increase under peak load; matches threshold. Need to validate whether this is noise or correlated with a specific compiler flag change.

2026-03-06 Performance Eng Rahul Mehta: Re-ran canary with kernel compiled without AVX512 fallback; P95 reduced by 1.2% but throughput dropped 4%. Suggest adding an 'opt-mode' field to manifest so we can publish alternative pins for different latency/cost tradeoffs.

2026-03-12 Diego Alvarez: Implemented gating rule engine and CI job that simulates telemetry diffs. Started wiring publisher to pin registry with 'canary' lifecycle. Next: UI affordance for manual approve/reject and runbook for fast rollback.
